interactions.summary: Jiang explains why he started with Paradiso: Virgil is an unreliable narrator, Inferno is a path of miseducation, and one must pass through untruth before reaching truth; a participant offers a partial gloss that Jiang rejects.
Jiang closes the session by insisting that students test his teaching against the actual text and by assigning the next five cantos for tomorrow.
A tiny closing aside from the room is followed by Jiang's thanks as the lecture ends.

claims.claim: Jiang argues that Virgil is an unreliable narrator and that readers misread the poem when they take Virgil's words as Dante's own final view of God, hell, and love.
Jiang says the road to truth requires first passing through untruth, because hell lies to you and purgatory slowly reveals the truth you could not reach directly.
Jiang treats the conventional practice of teaching only Inferno as fundamentally wrong because without the full arc to Paradise one cannot appreciate Dante's message.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang says Dante's real battle is to displace Virgil as poet of the universe.
signature_moments.source_phrase: Dante's real mission is to displace Virgil as the poet of the universe
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is a high-pressure lens claim about the poem's inner agon and will matter for the public read.

signature_moments.moment: Truth is only reachable by first embracing the lie and passing through miseducation.
signature_moments.source_phrase: you must embrace the lie, before you can actually seek the truth
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is one of the lecture's sharpest epistemic formulations and a likely episode anchor.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang applies this to Virgil, arguing that Virgil's speech in Inferno must be corrected by what Paradise later reveals.
Jiang's term for the necessary path through falsehood and wrong belief that prepares access to truth.
A teaching strategy justified by the need to hear Inferno against the corrective endpoint rather than in isolation.

chronology_notes.note: This final packet closes the June 20 lecture by turning the whole class into a method claim about reading Inferno only through the truth disclosed later in Paradise, then assigning the next cantos for the following session.

uncertainty_notes.note: The brief participant aside at the end is too clipped to carry semantic weight beyond signaling the lecture's close.
